questions.title: Count Doubling Loop Iterations
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int doubling_iterations(int n)

A profiling loop runs

    for (i = 1; i < n; i *= 2)

It must return exactly how many times the loop body executes for the given n.

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
One line with the iteration count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Stride Loop Step Count
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int stride_steps(int n, int k)

A loop runs

    for (i = 0; i < n; i += k)

It must return exactly how many times the loop body executes.

Input Format:
One line with n and the stride k.

Output Format:
One line with the step count.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 1000000

questions.title: Triangle Loop Work
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long triangle_work(int n)

A profiler watches the nested shape

    for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
        for (j = 0; j < i; j++)  /* work */

It must return the total number of inner-body executions, computed by actually counting the loops.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the total inner executions.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5000

questions.title: Halving Loop Count
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int halvings(int n)

A shrink loop runs

    while (n > 1) { n = n / 2; count++; }

It must return how many halving steps happen until n reaches 1 (n = 1 needs 0 steps).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the halving count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Shrinking Loop by Three
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int shrink_steps(int n)

A countdown loop runs

    for (i = n; i > 0; i -= 3)

It must return exactly how many times the loop body executes.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the step count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 3000000

questions.title: Worst Case Scan Comparisons
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int scan_comparisons(int n, int target_pos)

A linear scan checks slots 1, 2, 3, ... n in order and stops as soon as it finds the target. The target sits at 1-based position target_pos; when target_pos is 0 the target is absent and the scan checks every slot.

It must return the number of slot checks performed.

Input Format:
One line with n and target_pos.

Output Format:
One line with the number of comparisons.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000, 0 <= target_pos <= n

questions.title: Campus Application Growth Gap
questions.description:
Two campuses verify application pairs differently. Campus North runs a nested pairing pass over n applications (n * n operations); Campus South runs one sweep (n operations). The analytics page wants the gap between the two workloads.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long growth_gap(int n)

It must return (n * n) - n, the number of extra operations the nested pass performs.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the gap.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000

questions.title: Library Capacity Doublings
questions.description:
A library server starts with capacity 1 e-book and doubles its capacity until it can hold all n e-books. The ops dashboard wants the number of doublings and the final capacity.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void capacity_plan(int n, int *doublings, int *capacity)

It must store the doubling count into *doublings and the final capacity into *capacity. The harness prints both.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the doubling count, then the final capacity, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000

questions.title: Stack Frames for Recursive Cleanup
questions.description:
A cleanup routine calls itself on n / 2 until the value reaches 1 (a call with n <= 1 does no further calls). The memory planner wants the total number of stack frames, including the base call.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int stack_frames(int n)

frames(n) = 1 when n <= 1, otherwise frames(n) = 1 + frames(n / 2) (integer division).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the frame count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Trainer Guessing Lower Bound
questions.description:
A gym trainer guesses a secret weight between 1 and m. Each guess keeps only the half that can hold the answer, so the range shrinks as range = (range + 1) / 2 per guess until a single candidate remains.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int guess_steps(int m)

It must return the number of guesses until the range collapses to one candidate (0 guesses when m is already 1).

Input Format:
One line with m.

Output Format:
One line with the guess count.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 1000000000

questions.title: Key-Value Store Rehash Plan
questions.description:
A key-value store starts at capacity 8 and doubles its capacity whenever n would exceed it. The SRE dashboard wants the rehash (doubling) count and the final capacity.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void rehash_plan(int n, int *doublings, int *capacity)

It must store the doubling count into *doublings and the final capacity into *capacity. The harness prints both. When n fits within 8 there are 0 doublings and the capacity stays 8.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the doubling count, then the final capacity, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000

questions.title: Loop Shape Dominance Report
questions.description:
A profiler compares two loop shapes over n items: shape SQUARE performs n * n operations and shape CUBE performs n * n * n. The report shows both counts and which shape dominates (TIE when equal).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    const char *dominant_shape(int n, long long *sq, long long *cb)

It must store n * n into *sq and n * n * n into *cb, and return "SQUARE", "CUBE" or "TIE" (whichever matches the comparison). The harness prints all three values.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line: the square count, the cube count and the dominating shape name, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000

questions.title: Sensor Sampling Report
questions.description:
A sensor log holds n readings and a sampler inspects every k-th reading (indices 0, k, 2k, ...). The dashboard wants how many readings were sampled and how many were skipped.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void sample_report(int n, int k, int *samples, int *skipped)

It must store the sampled count into *samples and the skipped count (n - samples) into *skipped. The harness prints both.

Input Format:
One line with n and k.

Output Format:
One line with the sampled count, then the skipped count, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 1000000

questions.title: Auxiliary Space Ledger
questions.description:
Two array-reversal strategies are compared for an array of n ints: the copy strategy needs one extra array of n ints, while the in-place strategy needs only two index variables. The memory ledger reports both auxiliary footprints in bytes.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void space_report(int n, int *copy_bytes, int *inplace_bytes)

It must store n * sizeof(int) into *copy_bytes and 2 * sizeof(int) into *inplace_bytes. The harness prints both.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the copy footprint, then the in-place footprint, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000

questions.title: Guessing Game Lower Bound
questions.description:
Any strategy for a guessing game over the range 1..m needs at least ceil(log2(m + 1)) guesses in the worst case. Compute that lower bound by repeatedly halving: start with r = m and count one guess per halving step r = r / 2 while r stays above 0.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int lower_bound_guesses(int m)

Input Format:
One line with m.

Output Format:
One line with the lower bound.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 1000000000

questions.title: Triangle Work Budget
questions.description:
A batch planner can afford at most B operations, and processing n items costs the triangle amount n * (n - 1) / 2. Find the largest n whose cost still fits the budget.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int max_n_for_budget(long long B)

It must return the largest n >= 1 with n * (n - 1) / 2 <= B (n = 1 always fits since its cost is 0).

Input Format:
One line with the budget B.

Output Format:
One line with the largest feasible n.

Constraints:
0 <= B <= 1000000000000

questions.title: Amortized Rebuild Copy Ledger
questions.description:
A dynamic array starts at capacity 1 and doubles whenever it is full, copying every existing element on each rebuild. Inserting n elements triggers rebuilds at sizes 1, 2, 4, ... The ledger reports the total element copies caused by rebuilds and the final capacity.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void amortized_copies(int n, long long *copies, int *capacity)

Total copies = 1 + 2 + 4 + ... up to the largest rebuild triggered (the capacity just below n); *capacity is the first power of two >= n. For n = 1 there are no rebuilds (0 copies, capacity 1). The harness prints both.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the total copies, then the final capacity, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000

questions.title: Factorial Growth Threshold
questions.description:
A crypto drill needs the smallest k whose factorial k! strictly exceeds a limit L. The drill also reports k! itself so the threshold can be double-checked.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void factorial_threshold(long long L, int *k, long long *fact)

It must store the smallest k with k! > L into *k and that factorial into *fact (1! = 1, 2! = 2, 3! = 6, ...). The harness prints both.

Input Format:
One line with the limit L.

Output Format:
One line with k, then k!, space-separated.

Constraints:
0 <= L <= 1000000000000 (the answer k is at most 15)

questions.title: Nested Halving Work Count
questions.description:
A profiler watches this exact nested shape over n:

    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++)
        for (j = i; j > 0; j /= 2)  /* work */

It must return the total number of inner-body executions, computed by actually running the counting loops.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long nested_halving_work(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the total inner executions.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000

questions.title: Halving Sum Trace
questions.description:
A dashboard traces a value that is repeatedly halved (integer division) until it reaches 0, e.g. 10 -> 5 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0. The trace reports the sum of ALL values shown including the final 0, and the number of halving steps taken.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void halving_trace(int n, long long *sum, int *steps)

It must store the trace sum into *sum and the step count into *steps. The harness prints both. For n = 0 the trace shows only 0 (sum 0, steps 0).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the sum, then the step count, space-separated.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000
